m101.text: Thursday after school. The quiz papers are back.

m102b.text: One mark out of three? But my answer was right!

m201m.text: My answers used to lose marks too. Then I met the Genie in TheOneApp.

m202.text: A little dragonfly is hiding in this video. Can you spot it?

m203p.text: Dragonflies love windows and plants. Look outside!

m204.text: You against the Buddies! Lock in first with your fingers. One finger for every point.

m302p.text: The four parts of a full answer.

h501.text: Are you ready? Three! Two! One! Go!

m401.text: Here is the question. Mei Ling hangs two metal bars, X and Y, from strings. She brings the North pole of a magnet near each bar. Bar X moves away from the magnet. Bar Y moves towards the magnet. Which bar is a magnet? Explain your answer.

m402.text: Round one. Which answer gets full marks? One, Basil's. Two, Pip's. Three, Momo's. Show me your fingers!

m404b.text: One! I wrote X. X is right!

m405p.text: Two. Mine says like poles repel. That is the science!

m406m.text: Three. Mine has all four parts.

m501.text: Be an answer! Shrink down. Quietly.

m502.text: You are an empty answer line in a quiz paper. A red piece floats down and clicks into place. Bar X is a magnet.

m503.text: Then a blue piece: what the question shows you. A yellow piece: the science rule. And last, a green piece that joins them all to the question.

m504.text: The marker's pen comes down. Tick. Tick. Tick. Full marks!

m601.text: The answer is three: Momo's answer! Did you show three fingers? Put one finger up!

m602.text: Meet the CECL Genie. It shows us the four parts of a full answer.

m701b.text: So what did my answer miss?

m702.text: Look closer. Basil gave a Choice: bar X. That is the red part.

m703.text: But it moved is not enough. Which way did bar X move? Away from the magnet. That is the Evidence, and it comes from the question.

m704b.text: An open-ended question is a question you answer in your own sentences, such as: which bar is a magnet? Explain your answer.

m705.text: Your turn. What science rule explains why bar X moved away? Think.

m706m.text: Evidence is what the question shows you, such as: bar X moved away from the magnet!

m708.text: A full answer has four parts: Choice, Evidence, Concept and Link.

m801p.text: I know my Concept! Bar X moves away from the magnet.

m802.text: Something is not right. If you can spot it, cross your arms. Hold on!

m804b.text: Pip, that is the question's own words! That is Evidence. The Concept is the rule you remember: like poles repel.

m901p.text: So how does Momo's answer fit together?

m902.text: Look closer. Choice, in red: Bar X is a magnet.

m903.text: Evidence, in blue: When the North pole of the magnet was brought near bar X, bar X moved away.

m904.text: Concept, in yellow: Like poles repel. Only a magnet can be repelled by another magnet.

m905.text: Link, in green: Thus, bar X was repelled, so bar X is a magnet.

m906p.text: A concept is the science rule you remember, that is true every time, such as: like poles repel!

m907m.text: Bar Y moved towards it, but a magnet attracts magnetic materials too, so that does not show Y is a magnet.

m909.text: Evidence is what the question shows you. Concept is the science rule you remember.

m1001.text: Show me your score hand! Two fingers? You beat the Buddies. High five!

m1002.text: Did you spot the dragonfly? It was on a twig of the tree outside!

m1003b.text: Here is a fun fact! A dragonfly's huge eyes can see almost all the way round its head. It gathers evidence from every side!

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?

m1101b.text: Now I want to try a new question, all by myself!

m1102.text: Can you build a full answer too? Find out in Part Two!
